issues.description: Regex name HAS_TIME overstates what the /\dm?s/i prefilter actually proves.
issues.detail: The pattern matches any digit followed by 's' or 'ms' anywhere in the string, including substrings inside identifiers, URLs, or content() values. It is a cheap fast-reject heuristic, not a 'has time' predicate. Rename to LIKELY_HAS_TIME or MIGHT_CONTAIN_TIME, or anchor the regex on word boundaries.

issues.description: Missing comment documenting the prefilter's soundness invariant and its coupling to valueParser.
issues.detail: The optimization relies on an implicit contract: if valueParser would find a time node, the raw string contains \dm?s. That invariant lives in two separate concerns with no explicit link. A one-line comment ('cheap pre-filter; valueParser is the authority; intentionally loose') would prevent a future parser change from silently breaking the fast path.

issues.description: No benchmark or test evidence backs the performance claim.
issues.detail: The changeset asserts a perf fix but ships no before/after numbers and no fixture guarding regex regression. A one-line benchmark against the issue #6869 reproducer plus confirmation that existing behavior tests still pass would convert intuition into evidence for a hot-path regex in a linter rule.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts the patch as a small, well-scoped fast-path optimization: a cheap regex prefilter short-circuits the expensive valueParser call when no time-like token is present, with unchanged semantics. All three reviewers raise the same naming concern — HAS_TIME overstates what /\\dm?s/i proves, since it is a loose heuristic that admits false positives in identifiers, URLs, and similar substrings. They also converge on wanting an explicit comment stating the soundness invariant tying the prefilter to valueParser's notion of a time node. Knuth and Torvalds additionally flag the absence of benchmark numbers or a regression test backing the performance claim. Verdict: ACCEPT with cosmetic cleanups; no correctness blockers.
